_about: The pack's structures (docs/lived-in.md). tools/structures/build.py turns this into kubejs/data/pack/... and config/tfc_real_world/geography/pack/...; edit this, not the generated files. Procedural variants name a builder in shapes.py; hand-built variants name a file tools/structures/templates/<structure>/<variant>.nbt (a hand-built file also replaces a procedural variant of the same name). Structures without any template yet are skipped.

landforms.site: all biomes except oceans, lakes, rivers and ice sheets (computed)

loot_caps._about: Highest progression-checker step allowed per era (tools/quests/pack_query.py); unreachable items only when listed in allow_unreachable.

site_loot._about: Default chest loot for the ancient sites by era (a site's hand-built chests get pack:chests/site_<loot_era>).

sites._about: Real ancient sites at their coordinates (pack_world:geographic). The waypoint is always written; the site's structure only once its hand-built template exists in tools/structures/templates/site/<site>/. Biomes: the computed 'site' group.

npcs._about: Easy NPC presets (draft: author them in game with the config UI and export to tools/structures/npcs/<id>.npc.snbt, which then wins). Trades are barter in TFC goods; never food.

trader.name: Trader
trader.greeting: Salt, cloth, seed. Bring hides or worked copper and we'll talk. The river carries everyone past here sooner or later.
tips: Jute grows tall where it's warm and wet. Ret it, strip it, twist it: that's your rope and your sacks.
Seed keeps; grain rots. Trade for seed if you mean to stay.

hermit.name: Hermit
hermit.greeting: Green stain on a cliff means copper under it. Red earth, sometimes tin nearby. I stopped digging. You won't.
tips: Fire your clay slow, in a pit of straw and logs. A pot that cracks was fired wet.
Fruit trees take years. Plant them before you need them.

smith.name: Travelling Smith
smith.greeting: Clay first, then fire, then metal. Bring me tin and I'll show you what copper wants to be.
tips: A mould that cracks in the fire was wet. Dry it a day.
Copper alone is soft. Add tin, about one part in nine, and it bites.

_ported_begin: Sections below this line were added for the settlements port (tools/structures/villages.py, tfg_import.py).

regions._about: Hand-drawn culture zones as [latitude, longitude] polygons (or boxes [south, west, north, east]), read by pack_world:region through TFC: Real World's own projection (docs: tools/structures/villages.py, the placement spec). Ocean inside a polygon is harmless: the biome tag keeps structures on land. Starting points to edit, not borders; zones.png in the research folder draws them.

scandinavia.note: Denmark, Norway south of the Arctic coast, Sweden's coast and south. Not Finland, not the Sami interior.

steppe.note: Kazakh steppe, Mongolia, Inner Mongolia, northern Xinjiang, the Altai and Tuva. Not the Tibetan plateau, not Uzbekistan's oases.

arab_world.note: Maghreb to Mashriq and the Arabian peninsula. Not Iran, Turkey or the Sahel. The Amazigh highlands and Nubia are left to styles that don't exist yet.

malay_peninsula.note: The Malay peninsula south of the Thai border.

sumatra_east.note: The east and south coast of Sumatra (Malay Riau, Jambi, Palembang).

minang_west_sumatra.note: The Minangkabau highlands of West Sumatra, the only home of the rumah gadang.

atlantic_europe.note: Ireland and Britain, northern France, the Low Countries, Germany, Poland, the Alps' northern foothills.

mediterranean.note: The Roman Mediterranean: Iberia, southern France, Italy, the Balkan coast, Greece, Anatolia's coasts, the Levant, North Africa's coast.

settings._note: off = the villages are checked but nothing is written; climate = written with tfc:climate placement and plain jigsaw, loads on the pack's current jar; region (the live setting) = pack_world:region and pack_world:guarded_jigsaw (pack_world 1.2.0 or later). build.py --villages MODE overrides it.

lint._note: Besides TFC's blocks the villages may hold Framed Blocks and Roads and Roofs (the pack keeps both), vanilla water and torches (TFC's own torch burns out in a template) and the sixteen vanilla carpets (floor decoration, left as they are). Remove an entry to forbid it.

norse_farmer.name: Farmer
norse_farmer.greeting: Rye and barley and a short summer. We take what the ground gives and hope the frost holds off.
tips: Rye takes the cold that barley can't. Sow it early and keep the best ears back for seed.
Hay before the first snow, or the cattle won't see spring.

norse_weaver.name: Weaver
norse_weaver.greeting: Wool on the spindle all winter. By spring there's a bolt of cloth, if the light holds.
tips: Spin first; yarn weaves, raw fleece doesn't.
A bone needle outlasts silver. You'll see why in January.

norse_herder.name: Herder
norse_herder.greeting: Sheep and goats on the high pasture. They find the way home if you let them.
tips: Goats go where sheep won't. Keep both and nothing is wasted.
Trade in what keeps: hides, wool, bone. Meat doesn't.

norse_smith.name: Smith
norse_smith.greeting: Copper and tin I know. The cold doesn't trouble a good fire.
tips: Copper alone is soft. A ninth part tin and it holds an edge.
A mould that cracks in the fire was wet. Dry it a day.

arabic_potter.name: Potter
arabic_potter.greeting: Clay from the river bank, a day in the sun, a night in the kiln. Nothing else holds water like it.
tips: Dry the clay slowly in the shade. A pot that dries too fast cracks in the fire.
Fire clay for the kiln, plain clay for the pots.

arabic_merchant.name: Merchant
arabic_merchant.greeting: Salt from the pans, rope from the oasis, cloth from further than you've been. Sit; the shade is free.
tips: Salt keeps everything, including your goods. Never buy a long road without it.
A caravan that follows the wells outlives one that follows the map.

arabic_dyer.name: Dyer
arabic_dyer.greeting: Madder for the red, indigo for the blue, and a vat that never dries. Cloth takes colour better than people do.
tips: Wet the cloth well first or the colour goes on in patches.
Fix a dye with salt and it will outlast the cloth.

arabic_well_keeper.name: Well Keeper
arabic_well_keeper.greeting: Water is shared here, and counted. Draw what you need and leave the rope where it hangs.
tips: Dig where the green grows in the dry season. The water is under it.
A jug in the shade keeps the water cool all afternoon.

arabic_smith.name: Smith
arabic_smith.greeting: Bronze for the bowls and the blades. Bring tin; copper alone is only half a thing.
tips: Nine parts copper to one of tin makes bronze, and bronze hardens under the hammer.
Charcoal burns hotter when the fire is fed air; keep the bellows moving.

malay_cook.name: Cook
malay_cook.greeting: Rice on the fire, fish on the rack, chilli in the pot. Whatever you bring, there's room for it.
tips: Wet rice wants flooded ground. Dry rice wants nothing but rain.
Salt the fish the day you catch it and it will keep until the monsoon.

malay_boatwright.name: Boatwright
malay_boatwright.greeting: The tide takes what it likes and gives back what floats. Build for the second kind.
tips: Pitch and rope are half a boat. Wood is the rest.
Read the water before you leave the shore, not after.

malay_weaver.name: Weaver
malay_weaver.greeting: Cotton is for the dry months, the loom is for the wet ones. The cloth tells what the year was like.
tips: Spin the yarn tight and weave it slack; the other way round it tears.
Dye after weaving, not before.

malay_smith.name: Smith
malay_smith.greeting: A kris takes a month. A fishhook takes an afternoon. I'll start with the hook.
tips: Make the blade, then temper it; the other order only gets you a crooked knife.
Charcoal from hardwood, never softwood. It burns slower and hotter.

steppe_herder.name: Herder
steppe_herder.greeting: The flocks move; so do we. Today the grass is here.
tips: Mares' milk, sheep's wool, horse hides. A herd gives more than meat if you let it live.
Camp on the lee of a rise: the wind is the enemy before the wolf is.

steppe_feltmaker.name: Feltmaker
steppe_feltmaker.greeting: Wool, water, and everyone's feet. That's all felt is, and the tents stand on it.
tips: Beat the wool wet, roll it tight and keep rolling. It's the rolling that makes it hold.
Felt turns rain; grass doesn't.

steppe_bowyer.name: Bowyer
steppe_bowyer.greeting: Horn, sinew and wood, held together with glue and patience. The glue is the secret.
tips: Glue a bow in the dry season; the damp will undo it.
Straight arrows fly straight. There is no other secret.

steppe_elder.name: Elder
steppe_elder.greeting: Sit by the fire. The road is long and you've only seen the part in front of you.
tips: Water is the only border out here. Learn where it is and you won't need another map.
A guest is a guest for three days. After that, a neighbour.

temperate_farmer.name: Farmer
temperate_farmer.greeting: Wheat, rye and a field of beans. Come in if you've a mind to; there's water in the jug.
tips: Rotate your crops. Beans put back what the wheat takes out.
Straw for the roof, straw for the beds, straw for the barn. You'll never have enough.

temperate_shepherd.name: Shepherd
temperate_shepherd.greeting: The ewes are lambing. Mind the dog.
tips: Wool at midsummer, lambs in spring. Everything else is weather.
A flock turned into the stubble does the field a favour.

temperate_orchardist.name: Orchardist
temperate_orchardist.greeting: Apples take eight years to be worth the wait. I started early.
tips: Plant the sapling where it will have sun and room; it won't forgive a bad choice.
Graft or buy: seeds from a good apple make a poor tree.
